p:cNvPr.descr: Part C: A three-part structure illustrating the transcriptional attenuation in the trp operon. Starting from the top is part a, which shows a wide backwards S, starting from the top left and ending on the bottom right. The structure is labeled mRNA and starts with pppAAGUUCACGUAAAAAGGGUAUCGACA, all in green, and moving right at the top, is AUGAAAGCAAUUUUCGUACUGAAAGGUUGGUGGCGCACUUCC, all in purple, and labeled 1. Where the purple begins is labeled leader peptide, and below it the purple strand of letters is labeled Met-Lys-Ala-Ile-Phe-Val-Leu-Lys-Gly-Trp-Trp-Arg-Thr-Ser-(stop). The (stop) sequence of letters is UGA (from right to left) is shaded in red. Continuing after the (stop), the letters are AA, shaded in green, CGGGCAGUGUAUUCACCAUG (shaded in blue and labeled 2), followed by CGUAAAGCAAUCAG (shaded in green), and looping around to the bottom of the backwards S, AUACCCAGCCCGCC (shaded in yellow and labeled 3), UAAU (shaded in green), GAGCGGGCU (shaded in pink and labeled 4), and finally, UUUUUUUGAACAAAUUAGAGAAUAACAAUGCAAACA (shaded in green), with an arrow pointing right. At the fifth U in this section, it is labeled 139 above and the “site of transcription attenuation” below. Starting at the AAUGCAAACA, the first A is labeled 162 on top, and an arrow points up to the space after it, labeled, “End of leader region (trpL).” Below these letters are Met-Gln-Thr, followed by an arrow pointing right. Below that is Trp polypeptide. Next is part b, which has two drawings, one on top of the other. The first one shows a tan rectangular line that is labeled DNA at the left end. Inside the tan is labeled trpL, and as it extends right, it turns blue and splits into two strands, forming an eye-shape as it enters a purple folded structure with an opening on its right; this structure is RNA polymerase. At the outer opening on the right, the two blue strands become one again and exit RNA polymerase. Inside the center of the purple structure is a purple triangle, and below it, a slinky green line is seen, labeled from right to left, 3’, UUUUUUU. Bending down and right, the green turns to a pink segment, labeled 4, followed by a green U shape that connects the pink with the next shape, which is a yellow segment labeled 3 moving up and left. This is labeled Attenuator structure. To the left of this is another green segment, followed by a light blue segment labeled 2, a short red segment, a short green segment, a long purple segment labeled 1, and a short green end on the left, with a 5’. This is labeled mRNA. About halfway inside the purple segment are two short dashes with raised ends, labeled Trp codons. Next to them is a mushroom-type structure with a yellow cap labeled as ribosome and a tan bottom that sits around the purple, red, green, and blue segments. Pink letters, MKAIFVLKGWWRTS curve up onto the top of the ribosome. To the left of the letters, text reads, “Completed leader peptide.” Below this structure is a gray text box that reads, “When tryptophan levels are high, the ribosome quickly translates sequence 1 (open reading frame encoding leader peptide) and blocks sequence 2 before sequence 3 is transcribed. Continued transcription leads to attenuation at the terminator-like attenuator structure formed by sequences 3 and 4.” Below this is a similar drawing as what was just described, however, this time, there is a gray arrow pointing right from RNA polymerase. Also, the green slinky shape underneath the purple triangle in the RNA polymerase is elongated and no longer lettered, and extends all the way down and left, where it is labeled trp-regulated genes. To its left is the pink segment labeled 4, the green segment, and going up, the yellow segment labeled 3, another green segment that loops up, and going down, then the blue segment labeled 2. The short red and green segments are right below this part, and to their left is the purple segment with the Trp codons, labeled 1, followed by the green segment and a 5’ at its end. The same mushroom-type structure is still there, but has shifted over to the left of the purple segment, and this time, the pink letters that curve into its top have been cut off, showing only MKAIFVLKG. This is labeled as Incomplete leader peptide. The gray text box beneath this diagram states, “When tryptophan levels are low, the ribosome pauses at the Trp codons in sequence 1. Formation of the paired structure between sequences 2 and 3 prevents attenuation, because sequence 3 is no longer available to form the attenuator structure with sequence 4. The 2:3 structure, unlike the 3:4 attenuator, does not prevent transcription.” In part c, there are two structures, one top of the other. The first one, labeled 3:4 Pair (attenuator), shows a short green segment, followed by a yellow one moving right and up, then a green segment that loops and comes down on the right, followed by a pink segment that travels down, and then another green segment that moves down and right to complete the full loop. The first green section has the letters A and G, followed by the yellow, labeled 3 (AUACCCAGCCCGCC, with the second A labeled 110), followed by another green (UAAU), followed by pink, labeled 4 (GAGCGGGCU), followed by another green (UUUUUU). In the middle of the structure, bonds occur between the yellow left and pink right segments; the bonds are seen between C-G, G-C, C-G, C-G, C-G, C-G, G-C, and A-U. Below this is a 2:3 pair, which is represented as a snake-like structure that also shows a sequence of letters. Starting from the bottom left and traveling up on one side, there is AA (shaded green), CGGGCAGUGUAUUCACCAUG (shaded in blue with the fourth G labeled 80 and the fifth C labeled 90). Moving up and around and then to the right side is CGUAAAGCAAUCAG (shaded green, with the second G labeled 10). At the top of the structure (the snake’s head), there is bond between C and G, G and C, and U and U. The first bond occurs between two green sections, but the other two occur on a left blue and right green sections. Below the green segment is AUACCCAGCCCGCC (shaded yellow and labeled 3, with the second A labeled 110). This ends in a green shaded U. In the middle of the snake there is a C-G bond, a U-A bond, an A-U bond, a U-A bond, and a G-C bond; with the exception of the first one, which occurs between a blue left and a right green section, the rest of the bonds occur on a blue left and right yellow. At the bottom of the snake, the bonds occur between C-G, G-C, G-C, G-C, and C-G, also on blue left and right yellow sections.
